live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust-based ransomware service behind attacks on hospitals, casinos and councils
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, sold ransomware to affiliates from late 2021. It extorted victims through a leak site until law enforcement action and a reported exit scam in 2023 and 2024.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, BlackCat, Ambitious Scorpius, UNC4466 and Noberus.
It runs as a ransomware-as-a-service business, selling malware subscriptions to criminals. Cybernews says it was first observed in late 2021 and was noted for using the Rust programming language.

BleepingComputer says the operation is believed to be a rebrand of DarkSide and BlackMatter. S2W found that BlackCat's configuration fields match BlackMatter's, but found it difficult to conclude they are the same group.

BleepingComputer, citing the FBI, says the group breached over 60 entities from November 2021 to March 2022. It also says the FBI estimated at least $300 million in ransom payments from over 1,000 victims until September 2023.
A 2022 attack on Suffolk County disabled its 911 system and other services. DataBreaches reported that ALPHV/BlackCat claimed responsibility and showed screenshots of the county's backup systems.
In 2023 the group took credit for an attack on McLaren HealthCare, which runs 13 hospitals in Michigan. The company confirmed a ransomware event. The gang's claim of 6 TB of stolen data is its own.
Henry Schein, a dental and medical distributor, reported an incident in October 2023. A report says AlphV later claimed responsibility.

Australia's national cybersecurity coordinator said an April attack on the law firm HWL Ebsworth exposed data from 65 government agencies. Alphv claimed the attack, and that claim is the report's basis for naming the group.
BleepingComputer reported in July 2022 that ALPHV had added a search function to its leak site, making stolen data easier to find.

Sygnia attributed one 2023 intrusion to BlackCat or one of its affiliates. Access came through a compromised third-party vendor. The attacker used Cobalt Strike, copied data out with Rclone, then sent extortion emails.
The Register reported that ALPHV/BlackCat affiliates used paid ads for business software such as Slack and Cisco AnyConnect to lure victims into installing Nitrogen malware.

ReliaQuest says Scattered Spider gains access through alliances with ransomware operators including ALPHV. AttackIQ, restating an FBI and CISA advisory, says Scattered Spider has run extortion with BlackCat/ALPHV ransomware since April 2023.

In September 2023 AlphV said it kept administrator access to MGM Resorts' identity systems and launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors on September 11. These are AlphV's own unverified claims.
BleepingComputer reports that the FBI disrupted the gang in December 2023 and temporarily took down its Tor negotiation and leak sites.
In February 2024, unnamed sources linked the Change Healthcare attack to BlackCat. BleepingComputer could not confirm this, and BlackCat had not claimed the attack at that time.

In March 2024 BleepingComputer judged that the gang was running an exit scam. Its sites went offline, affiliates said they were not paid, and it offered its source code for $5 million. ALPHV told the report its infrastructure was seized, and Europol and the NCA denied involvement.
The U.S. State Department offered rewards of up to $10 million for information on people tied to the group, plus $5 million for people linked to its attacks.
Treat a leak-site claim as unconfirmed until the victim or investigators confirm it.
Check and limit what third-party vendors can reach in your network.
